---
title: "Summary fields"
---

This page is the field-by-field reference for the five Airtable tables that make up a summary.
For the order to fill them in, see [Adding a summary](adding-a-summary.qmd).

Field names here match Airtable exactly.
Hover over a field's name in Airtable to see a short description of it.

**Required** fields must be filled in before a summary can be published.
If one is empty, the summary shows *Needs fixing* and the Sync message names the field.

## Summaries

One row per summary.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Title** | Yes | The display name, e.g. "Social media". Usually the same as the exposure type. |
| **Status** | Yes | *Draft* (not on the website), *Preliminary* (published with a "not yet reviewed" banner) or *Reviewed* (checked by the review team). A blank Status counts as Draft. |
| **Slug** | Filled in by the sync | The page's web address (`…/evidence/<slug>`). Leave it blank for a new summary. **Never change it once the summary is published**: old links stop working. |
| **Exposure type** | Yes | One value from the [list below](#exposure-types). |
| **Screen content** | Yes, at least one | Tags for the kind of content: Educational, Entertainment, Social, Creative, Passive, Interactive. They drive the website's content filter. |
| **Audiences** | Yes, at least one | Teachers, Parents or Students. The website currently has teacher pages only; parent and student recommendations are stored for later. Only list an audience you have written recommendations for. |
| **Short summary** | Yes | One plain-language sentence of **at most 160 characters**, shown on the overview card. If the evidence is mixed, say so here. |
| **Overall impact** | Yes | Your judgement of the overall harm or benefit, −3 to +3. Not an average ([guidance](rating-the-evidence.qmd#the-overall-rating)). |
| **Overall confidence** | Yes | Your confidence in that overall judgement, 0 to 5. |
| **Last reviewed** | Yes | The date the ratings were last checked against the evidence. |
| **What is it?** | Yes | A definition of the exposure in one to three sentences. |
| **Meta-analyses** | Optional | Number of meta-analyses (and umbrella reviews) the summary draws on. |
| **Primary studies** | Optional | Number of underlying studies, where the reviews report it. |
| **Participants** | Optional | Total participants, where the reviews report it. |
| **About the evidence** | Optional | Two or three sentences on the evidence base: the kinds of study, who took part, and any important caveat. |
| **Unpublished sources** | Optional | Sources with no formal citation (e.g. an unpublished analysis), one per line. |
| **Findings** | Yes, at least one | The linked Findings rows. Their order here is their order on the website. |
| **How effects differ** | Optional | The linked Moderators rows, in display order. |
| **Recommendations** | At least one per audience listed | The linked Recommendations rows, in display order. If an audience in Audiences has no recommendations, the summary still publishes but the Sync message warns you. |
| **References** | Yes, at least one | The linked References rows. Their order here is their numbering on the website. |
| **Publish** | — | A button that opens the publishing page on GitHub ([how to publish](publishing.qmd)). |
| **Sync status**, **Sync message**, **Published slug**, **Last published** | Written by the sync | Read these after each run; never edit them. See [Publishing and fixing problems](publishing.qmd). |

## Findings

One row per **specific outcome**.
On the website, findings are grouped under their domain heading, in the order of the summary's Findings list.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Outcome** | Yes | The specific outcome, in a few words. Add a qualifier after a colon when a summary has several rows on the same outcome, e.g. "Depressive symptoms: time spent on social media" and "Depressive symptoms: problematic (compulsive) use". |
| **Evidence summary** | Yes | The one summary this finding belongs to. |
| **Domain** | Yes | One of the five [outcome domains](#outcome-domains). |
| **Impact** | Yes | −3 to +3, shown as e.g. "−2 · Moderate harmful" ([how to rate](rating-the-evidence.qmd#impact)). Required even when Evidence quality is 0: choose "0 · No clear relationship". |
| **Evidence quality** | Yes | 0 to 5, shown as e.g. "3 · Moderate confidence" ([how to rate](rating-the-evidence.qmd#evidence-quality)). **0** means not enough evidence to rate: the website then shows "Not enough evidence to rate yet" instead of an impact rating. |
| **Plain-language summary** | Yes | The finding in one or two plain sentences, with no statistics. |
| **Evidence detail** | Yes | The supporting detail: effect sizes, number of studies and participants, study designs and caveats. |
| **Order** | Optional | Leave blank to use the order of the summary's Findings list. |

## Moderators

One row per factor the effect differs by.
These make up the "How effects differ" section.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **What the evidence shows** | Yes | How the effect differs, in plain language, e.g. "Links with poorer mental health were stronger in samples with a higher proportion of girls and women." |
| **Evidence summary** | Yes | The one summary this row belongs to. |
| **Moderator** | Yes | One of the [moderators below](#moderator-list). Each can appear only once per summary. |
| **Order** | Optional | Leave blank to use the order of the summary's "How effects differ" list. |

## Recommendations

One row per strategy, for one audience.
These make up the "What can I do?" section.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Title** | Yes | The strategy as an action, e.g. "Help students recognise unhealthy social media use". |
| **Evidence summary** | Yes | The one summary this strategy belongs to. |
| **Audience** | Yes | Teachers, Parents or Students. |
| **What this looks like** | Yes | Specific things to do, **one per line**. The website adds the bullets. |
| **Why this works** | Optional | One or two sentences linking the strategy to a finding or moderator. Leave it blank if there is no clear link to the evidence. |
| **Order** | Optional | Leave blank to use the order of the summary's Recommendations list. |

## References

One row per citation.
This is the only table whose rows can be shared: a reference cited in several summaries is **one row linked to each of them**.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **Citation** | Yes | The full reference in APA 7 style, with the DOI as a link (`https://doi.org/…`). |
| **Evidence summaries** | Yes | Every summary that cites this reference. |
| **Source note** | Optional | A short description shown next to the reference in "About the evidence", e.g. "Meta-analysis: 63 studies, 144 effect sizes" or "Umbrella review: re-analysed estimates for children and adolescents". |

Because a reference can be shared, **unlink** it from your summary to remove it.
Deleting the row removes it from every summary that cites it.

## Controlled lists

The dropdowns in Airtable only offer values the website accepts.
They are the current lists; the lists on this page are for orientation and were last checked in October 2026.

If you need a value that isn't offered, ask the platform maintainer.
Adding one needs a change to the platform's code as well as to Airtable.
Don't type a new option into a dropdown yourself: the summary will show *Needs fixing* until the code knows about it.

### Exposure types

| Recreational | Educational & purposeful |
|--------------|--------------------------|
| General screen time | Media literacy education |
| TV & video games | Reading on screens |
| Violent & frightening media | Digital literacy programmes |
| Prosocial media | Maths software & games |
| Social media | Game-based learning |
| Cyberbullying | Educational technology in the classroom |
| Mobile phones & tablets | Language learning technology |
| Food & drink advertising | Immersive technology (AR/VR) |
| | Programming & coding |
| | Cognitive training |
| | Educational TV & video |
| | Active video games & gamified exercise |
| | Digital health & wellbeing programmes |

The two groups are used by the website's "type of use" filter.
A new exposure type also needs a group.

### Outcome domains

| Domain | Typical outcomes |
|--------|------------------|
| Learning & cognition | Academic achievement, literacy, maths, language, executive functions, creativity, computational thinking |
| Mental health | Depressive symptoms, anxiety, fear, emotion regulation, self-esteem, coping |
| Wellbeing | Sleep, life satisfaction, social support |
| Behaviour & engagement | Aggression, behaviour problems, ADHD symptoms, prosocial behaviour, motivation and enjoyment, school attendance |
| Physical health | Physical activity, fitness, motor skills, body weight, diet and food choices |

### Moderators {#moderator-list}

Age; Sex; Socioeconomic status; Setting; Dose / duration; Type of activity or content; Subject area; Learner needs; Ethnicity or culture; Adult involvement.
